reader_usefulness.location: Entire report, lines 1–292; research brief, effective requirements and scope decisions read. Especially memory/latency envelopes (15–75), the three workload chapters (77–178), data and integration boundaries (180–210), accepted-task economics and fit matrix (212–268), and interpretation appendix (271–291).
reader_usefulness.basis: The report gives device-product leaders and deployment engineers a usable path from workload requirements to local, cloud or hybrid architecture. It starts with acceptable completed tasks, then explains the separate weight, working-memory and KV budgets with a phone/PC context example. It connects phase rates to output length and usable-result latency, carries the Android performance-lock limitation into derived interactive timing, and keeps burst measurements separate from sustained service. Quantization and runtime examples explicitly include quality and backend limitations. Private-document retrieval, short interactive generation and frequent speech each have a concrete pipeline, failure boundary and conditional recommendation; speech segmentation, queue freshness, noise quality and endpoint power are not inferred from text-token throughput. The hardware–model–task matrix preserves the evidence differences among the S24, M4 Pro, Surface and Orin configurations instead of inviting an unsupported speed ranking. Readers can tell which memory, transfer, power and economic numbers are assumptions, which are historical measurements, and which deployment measurements are still missing. Privacy routing covers excerpts, transcripts, tools, logs and retention; system-API eligibility, foreground restrictions and version transitions remain attached to the proposed uses. Accepted-task cost distinguishes existing devices from dedicated endpoints, fixed engineering cost, fallback and correction work, with sensitivity examples and explicit scenario limits. The concluding rules follow from these trade-offs and provide concrete choices for offline, sensitive, bursty difficult and continuous workloads. I found no reader-understanding or decision-use defect requiring revision. This is a reader-usefulness judgment from the current task and complete report, not a new factual audit, source-verification claim or inference experiment.
